title: Designing AI Agents: 4 Lessons from China’s Qwen Agent
partialText: A study of Qwen's AI agent reveals 4 design lessons: support discoverability, reuse familiar patterns, handle personal data carefully, and protect user autonomy.

title: UX Writing: FAQs from Practitioners
partialText: Get answers to frequently asked questions about UX writing from attendees of NN/G’s Writing Compelling Digital Copy course.

title: Selection Criteria: How to Pick Your Participants
partialText: Rigorous selection criteria protect study validity. Learn how to define inclusion, exclusion, and diversity criteria to avoid costly misrecruits.

title: Information Seeking in China: A Different Ecosystem, Familiar Behavior
partialText: Information seeking in China is driven by mobile social-media apps. But how users prompt and engage with genAI mirrors what we've seen in the West.

title: 10 Guidelines for Designing Your Site’s AI Chatbots
partialText: Helpful site-specific AI chatbots clearly state their capabilities, offer relevant prompt suggestions, and quickly signal they know what users are looking at.

title: Why User Panels Fail
partialText: User panels can deteriorate in predictable ways, introducing bias and reducing their effectiveness for ongoing research.

title: Boost Design Autonomy with an Information Pipeline
partialText: A four-step framework for building influence over product direction by closing the information gaps that large, complex organizations create.

title: Less Chat, More Answer: Site AI Chatbots Need to Get to the Point
partialText: Users turn to site-specific chatbots for quick answers, not a conversation. Design responses that are direct, scannable, and easy to expand when needed.

title: Handmade Designs: The New Trust Signal
partialText: In an era of AI-generated-everything, AI-fatigued users want designs that look like they were made by a person.

title: AI Agents as Users
partialText: AI agents now interact with digital interfaces alongside humans. Designing for both requires rethinking what "user" means and prioritizing accessibility.

title: AI Can Help with Survey Writing, But It Still Requires Human Expertise
partialText: AI can produce polished survey drafts quickly, but experienced human review is still needed to catch subtle survey-design flaws that weaken data quality.

title: A Concrete Definition of an AI Agent
partialText: An AI agent pursues a goal by iteratively taking actions, evaluating progress, and deciding next steps. Useful agents must be reliable, adaptive, and accurate.

title: GenUI vs. Vibe Coding: Who’s Designing?
partialText: With generative UI, the AI system decides to generate an interactive element or entire product in response to a user need. Vibe coding is when users request the AI to build it.

title: Minimum Viable Product (MVP): Definition
partialText: MVPs are learning tools that test whether an idea is valuable to users.

title: New Artificial Intelligence Specialty for UX Certification

title: The 3 C’s of Informational Microcopy
partialText: Well-written informational microcopy should be clear, concise, and have character.

title: What Is Your Site's AI Chatbot for? Users Can't Tell
partialText: Users see little reason to use site AI chatbots. To prove their value, chatbots must solve problems that existing site features don't.
